questions.q: If point $D$ divides the base $B^{\prime}$; of a $\triangle A B C$ in the ratio $n: m$, then the value of $m B D^2+n C D^2+(m+n) A D^2$ is
questions.solution:
$m B D^2+n C D^2+(m+n) A D^2=m B D^2+n C D^2+m A D^2+n A D^2$
$\begin{aligned} & =m\left(B D^2+A D^2\right)+n\left(C D^2+A D^2\right) \\ & =m\left(A B^2+2 D M \cdot D B\right)+n\left(A C^2-2 D M \cdot D C\right) \\ & =m A B^2+m \cdot 2 D M \cdot D B+n A C^2-n \cdot 2 D M \cdot D C \\ & =m A B^2+n A C^2+2 D M(m D B-n D C) \\ & =m A B^2+n A C^2+2 D M(m n-n m) \\ & =m A B^2+n A C^2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The value of the angle between two straight lines $y=(2-\sqrt{3}) x+5$ and $y=(2+\sqrt{3}) x-7$ is
questions.solution:
Given equation of straiaht lines are
$y=(2-\sqrt{3}) x+5$
and $\quad y=(2+\sqrt{3}) x-7$
On comparing with $y=m x+c$, we get
$m_1=2-\sqrt{3}$
and $\quad m_2=2+\sqrt{3}\therefore \quad \tan \theta=\frac{m_2-m_1}{1+m_1 m_2}=\frac{2+\sqrt{3}-(2-\sqrt{3})}{1+(2-\sqrt{3})(2+\sqrt{3})}=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{1+(4-3)}=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{1+4-3}\Rightarrow \quad \tan \theta=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{2}=\sqrt{3}\Rightarrow \quad \theta=60^{{}^{\circ}}$

Then $a+b=4\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad $\begin{array}{l}\Rightarrow \\ \Rightarrow \\ \therefore \quad $\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{4-a}=$1 \\ \Rightarrow \quad x(4-a)+y a\end{array}$ \\ & \Rightarrow a(4-a)\end{aligned}$
This passes through $\left(\frac{9}{2},-5\right)$.
$\begin{array}{ll}\therefore & \frac{9}{2}(4$-a)-5 a=a(4-a) \\ \Rightarrow & 36-9 a-10 a=8 a-2 a^2 \\ \Rightarrow & 2 a^2-27 a+36=0 \\ \Rightarrow & a=12 $\text{$ or $}\frac{3}{2}\text{ but }$ a \neq 12 \\ \therefore & a=$\frac{3}{2}$ \Rightarrow b=$\frac{5}{2}$\end{array}$\therefore$ Required equation is
$\begin{array}{cc}& \frac{2 x}{3}+\frac{2 y}{5} =1 \\ \Rightarrow \quad & 10 x+6 y=15\end{array}$

Let $P M=r$. Then, the coordinates of $M$ given by $\frac{x-1}{\cos \frac{3 \pi}{4}}=\frac{y-1}{\sin \frac{3 \pi}{4}}=r$ is $\left(1-\frac{r}{\sqrt{2}}, 1+\frac{r}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\because M$ lies on $2 x-3 y-4=0$. $\therefore \quad 2\left(1-\frac{r}{\sqrt{2}}\right)-3\left(1+\frac{r}{\sqrt{2}}\right)-4=0\begin{array}{rlrl}\Rightarrow & 2-\frac{2 r}{\sqrt{2}}-3-\frac{3 r}{\sqrt{2}}-4 & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & -5-\frac{5 r}{\sqrt{2}} & =0 \\ \Rightarrow & & r & =-\sqrt{2}\end{array} Hence, $P M=$\sqrt{2}$

questions.solution:
Variable line is $\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{b}=1$ ....(i)
Any line perpendicular to (i) and passing througn tne oriain will be

which is a circle.

questions.solution:
Since, the lines $3 x+4 y+2=0$ and $3 x+4 y+5=0$ are on the same side of the origin. The distance between these lines is $5-2=3$.
And the line $3 x+4 y+2=0$ and $3 x+4 y-5=0$ are opposite side of the origin, The distance between these lies is 7.
Hence, required ratio is $3: 7$.

questions.q: If $A(-1,3,2), B(2,3,5)$ and $C(3,5,-2)$ are vertices of a $\triangle A B C$, then angles of $\triangle A B C$ are
questions.solution:
Given vertices of a $\triangle A B C$ are
$\begin{aligned} & A(-1,3,2), B(2,3,5) \text{$ and $} C(3,5,-2) . \\ & \text{ Now DR's of } A B=(2+1,3-3,5-2)=(3,0,3) \\ & \text{ DR's of } B C=(3-2,5-3,-2-5)=(1,2-7) \\ & \text{ and DR's of } C A=(-1-3,3-5,2+2) \\ &=(-4,-2,4)\end{aligned}$
Now, the angle between A B and B C$,
\begin{aligned} \cos B & =\frac{|3 \times 1+0 \times 2+3 \times(-7)|}{\sqrt{3^2+0^2+3^2} \sqrt{1^2+2^2+(-7)^2}} \\ & =\frac{|3+0-21|}{\sqrt{9+0+9} \sqrt{1+4+49}} \\ & =\frac{18}{3 \sqrt{2} \times 3 \sqrt{6}}=\frac{2}{2 \sqrt{3}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}$
angle between $B C and C A$,
$\begin{aligned} \cos C & =\frac{|1 \times(-4)+2(-2)+(-7)(4)|}{\sqrt{1^2+2^2+(-7)^2} \sqrt{(-4)^2+(-2)^2+(4)^2}} \\ & =\frac{|-4-4-28|}{\sqrt{1+4+49} \sqrt{16+4+16}} \\ & =\frac{36}{\sqrt{54} \sqrt{36}}=\frac{36}{3 \sqrt{6} \times 6} \\ & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}$
and angle between A C$ and A B$,
$\cos A=\frac{|-4 \times 3+(-2) \times 0+4 \times 3|}{\sqrt{(-4)^2+(-2)^2+(4)^2} \sqrt{3^2+0^2+3^2}}=|0|\Rightarrow A=90^{{}^{\circ}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the axes be turned through an angle $\tan ^{-1} 2$. What does the equation $4 x y-3 x^2=a^2$ become?
questions.solution:
Here, $\tan \theta=2$
So, $\cos \theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}, \sin \theta=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$
For $x and y$, we have $x=X \cos \theta-Y \sin \theta=\frac{X-2 Y}{\sqrt{5}}$ and $y=X \sin \theta+Y \cos \theta=\frac{2 X+Y}{\sqrt{5}}$
The equation $4 x y-3 x^2=u^2$ reduces to
$\frac{4(X-2 Y)}{\sqrt{5}} \cdot \frac{(2 X+Y)}{\sqrt{5}}-3\left(\frac{X-2 Y}{\sqrt{5}}\right)^2=a^2\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad 4\left(2 X^2-2 Y^2-3 X Y\right) -3\left(X^2-4 X Y+4 Y^2\right)=5 a^2\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad 5 X^2-20 Y^2=5 a^2\Rightarrow \quad X^2-4 Y^2=a^2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the straight line $a_1 x+b_1 y+c_1=0$, $a_1 x+b_1 y+c_2=0, \quad a_2 x+b_2 y+d_1=0$ and $a_2 x+b_2 y+d_2=0$ are the sides of rhombus, then
questions.solution:
Since, given straight lines are the sides of a rhombus. Therefore, distance between the parallel lines
$a_1 x+b_1 y+c_1=0, a_1 x+b_1 y+c_2=0$ and
$a_2 x+b_2 y+d_1=0, a_2 x+b_2 y+d_2=0$ must be equal
$\therefore \frac{\left|c_1-c_2\right|}{\sqrt{a_1^2+b_1^2}}=\frac{\left|d_1-d_2\right|}{\sqrt{a_2^2+b_2^2}}\Rightarrow\left(a_2^2+b_2^2\right)\left(c_1-c_2\right)^2=\left(a_1^2+a_1^2\right)\left(d_1-d_2\right)^2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the straight line which passes through the intersection of the lines $x-y-1=0$ and $2 x-3 y+1=0$ and is parallel to $x$-axis, is
questions.solution:
The equation of any line through the point of intersection of the lines $x-y-1=0$ and $2 x-3 y+1=0$ is
$(x-y-1)+\lambda(2 x-3 y+1)=0\Rightarrow (2 \lambda+1) x-y(3 \lambda+1)+(\lambda-1)=0...(i)$
The line in Eq. (i) will be parallel to $x$-axis, if it is of the form $y=$ constant, therefore coefficient of $x$ in Eq. (i) $=0$
ie, $2 \lambda+1=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=-\frac{1}{2}$
On putting $\lambda=-\frac{1}{2}$ in Eq. (i), we get $y=3$
This is the equation of the required line.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The distance of the point $(2,3)$ from the line $2 x-3 y+9=0$ measured along a line $x-y+1=0$ is
questions.solution:
The slope of the line $x-y+1=0$ is 1 . So, it makes an angle of $45^{{}^{\circ}}$ with $x$-axis. The equation of a line passing through $(2,3)$ and making an angle of $45^{{}^{\circ}}\frac{x-2}{\cos 45^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{y-3}{\sin 45^{{}^{\circ}}}=r$ Coordinates of any point on this line are $\left(2+r \cos 45^{{}^{\circ}}, 3+r \sin 45^{{}^{\circ}}\right)$ or, $\left(2+\frac{r}{\sqrt{2}}, 3+\frac{r}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ If this point lies on the line $2 x-3 y+9=0$, then $4+\sqrt{2} r-9-\frac{3 r}{\sqrt{2}}+9=0\Rightarrow r=4 \sqrt{2}$ Alternate Method
Since the point $(2,3)$ lies on the line $x-y+1=0$. Therefore the distance from $(2,3)$ to the line $2 x-3 y+9=0$ along the line $x-y+1=0$ is equal to the distance between the points $(2,3)$ and intersection point of $2 x-3 y+9=0 and x-y+1=0$ ie, $(6,7)$. Hence required distance, $\begin{aligned} & d=\sqrt{(6-2)^2+(7-3)^2}=\sqrt{32} \\ & d=4 \sqrt{2} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a tree on a vertices there is exactly one vertex with degree 2 and remaining vertices are of degree either 1 or 3. Then the number of pendant vertices is
questions.solution:
Total degree $=2(n-1)=2 n-2$
Let $p$ be the number of pendant vertices. Then $(n-p-1)$ are vertices with degree 3, one vertex of degree 2. Total degree $=2+p+3(n-p-1)\Rightarrow 2 n-2=-1-2 p+3 n\Rightarrow p=\frac{n+1}{2}=\frac{9+1}{2} \quad(\because n=9$ given)
$=5$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A line passing through origin and is perpendicular to two given lines $2 x+y+6=0$ and $4 x+2 y-9=0$. The ratio in which the origin divides this line, is
questions.solution:
Equation of line perpendicular to $2 x+y+6=0$ and passes through origin is $x-2 y=0$
Now, the point of intersection of $2 x+y+6=0 and x-2 y=0$ is $\left(-\frac{12}{5},-\frac{6}{5}\right)$
Similarly, the point of intersection of $x-2 y=0 and 4 x+2 y-9=0$ is $\left(\frac{9}{5}, \frac{9}{10}\right)$.
Let the origin divide the line $x-2 y=0$ in the ratio $\lambda: 1\therefore \quad x=\frac{\frac{9}{5} \lambda-\frac{12}{5}}{\lambda+1}=0$\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & $\frac{9}{5}$ \lambda=$\frac{12}{5}$ \\ \Rightarrow & \lambda=$\frac{12}{9}=\frac{4}{3}$\end{array}

questions.q: The line $x+2 y=4$ is translated parallel to itself by 3 unit in the sense of increasing $x$ and then rotated by $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ in the anti-clockwise direction about the point where the shifted line cuts the $x$-axis. The equation of the line in the new position is
questions.solution:
The equation of a line parallel to $x+2 y=4$ is $x+2 y=k$. Since, the distance between these two lines is 3 , therefore
$\begin{array}{ll} & \frac{k}{\sqrt{1+4}}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{1+4}}=3 \\ \Rightarrow & k=4+3 \sqrt{5}\end{array}
This shifted line cuts $ x$-axis at $(k, 0). After rotation the $slope of the line is \tan  \left(\theta-30^{{}^{\circ}}\right), where $\tan \theta=$ (slope of
$(x+2 y=4)=-$\frac{1}{2}$\therefore$ The equation of the line in the new position is
$\begin{aligned} & y-0=$\tan\left(\theta-30^{{}^{\circ}}\right)$(x-k) \\ \Rightarrow \quad & y=$\tan\left(\theta-30^{{}^{\circ}}\right)(x-k)\end{aligned}$
where $k=4+3 \sqrt{5}$
